Molecular-chain Rg is not established. A numerical Guinier fit can describe a scattering feature, domain or aggregate. Polymer identity, physical state, concentration, contrast and background treatment are needed to assign it to individual chains. Rejected candidate values below are diagnostic slopes, not extracted polymer sizes.

No frames were averaged. Counts indicate numerical screening outcomes, not distinct physical samples or independent replicates.

Specific observations: MAXS1 has four 857-point curves with declared Å⁻¹ units. Their low-q upturn and curved Guinier plots do not support a defensible Rg. The final four T0 intensities collapse near zero at q ≥ 0.88682 Å⁻¹: inspect this terminal anomaly before wide-q modelling.

The archive contains Samples 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10 and 11; Samples 4, 8 and 9 are absent. All 4,635 DAT profiles were screened, and seven aggregate tables were skipped to avoid duplication. Zero/zero masks precede the usable signal; the first nonzero q varies from 0.1528977 to 0.2046477 in unspecified units. No q conversion was inferred from the numbers or filenames.

Sample 7 shows decreasing low-q scattering but fails the low-q/qRg checks. Most other archive groups show poor low-q linearity, endpoint sensitivity or residuals inconsistent with the provisional error column. These are screening findings, not diagnoses of polymer chemistry, aggregation or sample quality.

What the software does

The numerical engine reads q, I and optional uncertainty, identifies no-data masks, screens a constrained set of low-q Guinier windows, calculates Rg and uncertainty, and checks range, statistical significance, residual curvature and endpoint stability. Every curve retains its status, reasons, source and diagnostic candidate. Files with unknown q units retain native lengths and cannot produce unconditional nanometre results.

ln I(q) = ln I(0) − q² Rg² / 3 and Rg = √(−3 × slope). Supplied errors are used through σ(log I) ≈ σ(I)/I. Without errors, regression uncertainty measures scatter about the line only. It excludes calibration, subtraction, model selection, covariance between bins and physical-model uncertainty.

Defaults are conservative engineering checks: qmax·Rg ≤ 1, qmin·Rg ≤ 0.5, sufficient points and q-span, meaningful negative slope, no strong curvature and stable endpoints. These checks are heuristics, not a universal certification of Guinier validity. Only a small near-origin search is allowed to avoid finding accidental linear segments at high q. Candidate selection and thresholds are available in core.py.

Only the numerical report determines whether an apparent scattering Rg is supported. Rejected candidate values must not be reported as measured polymer-chain sizes.

Confirm q units, polymer identity, sample state, concentration, solvent/contrast, background subtraction and frame-to-time mapping. Unknown q units prevent a physical size conversion.

A chain Rg requires evidence that the scattering comes from individual chains. Peak spacings and correlation lengths are different structural quantities.

The included prompt can be reviewed and sent to a configured model using an explicit LLM action.

The optional adapter can send compact fit summaries to a local Ollama model or an explicitly configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It explains results and requests missing metadata; it cannot modify the numerical result file. This is an inference integration, not an LLM trained on the uploaded experiments. Online provider execution is separate from numerical tests.

WAXS and model extensions

The package includes an exploratory peak/d-spacing function and an optional Debye ideal-coil fit. Peak spacing d = 2π/q is distinct from Rg. Peak detection requires a user-selected physical q interval and confirmation of units; it does not identify a crystalline phase, quantify crystallinity or estimate Scherrer sizes automatically. The uploaded archive has only SAXS-named 1D curves and unspecified q units, so WAXS coverage cannot be verified. MAXS1 reaches 0.88988 Å⁻¹ and is not a complete conventional wide-angle pattern.

A Debye fit is conditional on ideal Gaussian-chain scattering and cannot rescue an unresolved Guinier result by itself. Constant background, form-factor amplitude and Rg can be highly correlated without a measured plateau. No forced Debye estimate is promoted to a molecular Rg in this report.

Information needed for physical interpretation

  • Polymer/sample mapping and whether each is a dilute solution, gel, film or bulk material.
  • Archive q units, instrument calibration, uncertainty-column definition and any desmearing.
  • Solvent, concentration, transmission normalization and sample/solvent/cell background protocol.
  • Meaning of frame indices and T0/T24/T48/T72; exposure duration and damage or processing history.
  • If possible, lower-q measurements and a dilution series to distinguish chains, interactions and aggregates.
